subject: maths
question:
The internal radius of a metallic pipe is 2 cm and its external radius is 2.7 cm. If the length of the pipe is 10 cm, then find the volume of the metal used for this pipe. 

 (right. Use left.pi=(22)/(7))
solution:
**Given:**

Internal radius of the pipe (r₁) = 2 cm.

External radius of the pipe (r₂) = 2.7 cm.

Length of the pipe (h) = 10 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of the metal used = Volume of the external cylinder - Volume of the internal cylinder

Volume of the cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

Volume of the external cylinder = πr₂²h

Volume of the internal cylinder = πr₁²h

Volume of the metal used = πr₂²h - πr₁²h

Volume of the metal used = πh(r₂² - r₁²)

r₂=2.7 {cm}, r₁=2 {cm}, h=10 {cm}

Volume of the metal used = (22/7) × 10 × (2.7² - 2²)

⇒ Volume of the metal used = (22/7) × 10 × (7.29 - 4)

⇒ Volume of the metal used = (22/7) × 10 × 3.29

⇒ Volume of the metal used = 22 × 4.7

⇒ Volume of the metal used = 103.4 cm³

**The correct answer is option 4.**
